title.narrative: Output 1.3. Increased institutional capacity and resilience of labour administrations

description.narrative:
In 2022, the Ministry of Labour established a Better Work Unit within its structure and selected it inspectors for the unit in April 2022. The Ministry appointed the head of the unit in September 2022.
In October 2022, the Ministry of Labour provided labour inspectors with body work cameras and established a relevant control room, which had contributed to automating inspection procedures and implementing the e-government vision, and, by having audio-visual records of all inspection visits, improved interactions between inspectors, workers, employers, and enhance transparency, accountability and quality of labour inspection. With the support from the United States and Canada, the ILO supported the establishment of the Unit and enhanced the capacity of its staff and other labour inspectors through training, joint visits, and the secondment/capacity building programme, which included a specialized course in March 2022 on behavioural change, including emotional intelligence, communication skills and self development. The ILO advised the Ministry of Labour on the relevant technical specifications, procured the 180 cameras and other relevant equipment for them and provided technical support and guidance on regulating the proper and effective use of those cameras.

Output 7.2. Increased capacity of Member States to ensure safe and healthy working conditions

description.narrative: The Ministry of Labour and the Social Security Corporation developed and launched the National Occupational Safety and Health Strategy which was endorsed by the Cabinet in May 2023. The Ministry of Labour updated two Occupational Safety and Health regulations, including Regulation No. 32 of 2023 on Preventive and Curative Medical care for Workers in Enterprises in May 2023, and also the Regulation No. 33, on the Establishment of the Occupational Safety and Health Committees and Appointment of Occupational Safety and Health Supervisors in the Enterprises in July 2023. With the support from the United States and Canada, the ILO supported Ministry of Labour and the Social Security Corportation in organizing a capacity-buidling programme on developing national Occupational Safety and Health profiles, policies and programmes in line with the relevant International Labour Standards. The ILO also provided technical inputs for draftng the strategy and organizing several tripartite and consultative activities to get comments and inputs from relevant partners and stakehilders. The ILO delivered a training course on the UK- based National Examination Board in Occupational Safety and Health (NEBOSH, IG1 and IG2), which was delivered to 20 labour inspectors in the last quarter of 2022.
